title: Usernames are unique regardless of case

findings.label: intended
findings.why: Announced in the PR description: "Usernames now have to differ by more than letter case: you can't register `Susan` if `susan` exists.". The description announces case-insensitive uniqueness for usernames, so updating a username to a case-variant of an existing username (e.g., 'ALICE' when 'alice' exists) should now be rejected with 400 instead of accepted with 200.

findings.head: {"username": "alice"}
findings.label: regression
findings.why: The description announces that case-conflicting updates are rejected (400), so the PUT request should fail and the username should remain unchanged; the observed change shows the GET response username changed from 'ALICE' to 'alice', which contradicts the announced rejection behavior.

findings.head: {"errors.json.username": ["Use a different username."]}
findings.label: intended
